# Gating Functions

![Gating Functions function icon](../../../../assets/function-icons/functions/math/gating/00_Repertoire%20Gating%20functions.svg)

[Mathematics functions](../index.md) · [All functions](../../index.md)

Browse Spike, Square and Step: three pure numeric gating functions of one required argument x. Classic LabVIEW documents scalar DBL; FROG adds real numeric-tree overloads and explicit IEEE conventions. No verified NXG overload, time source, state or waveform output.

## Browse this palette

This entry opens a palette folder; it is not an executable dataflow function.

| Entry | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [Spike](../../math/gating/spike.md) | Returns 1 for 0≤x&lt;1 and 0 elsewhere; a nonperiodic unit rectangular pulse. Input x; output spike(x). Spike(±0)=1; Spike(1)=0; Spike(±Infinity)=+0. NaN produces NaN. Example: Spike(0.25)=1; Spike(1)=0. |
| [Square](../../math/gating/square.md) | Returns a numeric 0/1 pulse of period 2: 1 on [2n,2n+1) and 0 elsewhere, also for negative x. This is the Gating function, distinct from arithmetic x×x. Input x; output square(x). Square(±0)=1; even integers give 1 and odd integers give 0 after numeric conversion. Square(±Infinity)=NaN. NaN produces NaN; all zero outputs are positive. Example: Square(-2)=1; Square(-1)=0; Square(-0.5)=0. |
| [Step](../../math/gating/step.md) | Returns 0 for negative x and 1 for positive or zero x. The value at zero is exactly 1; this is a pure unit step, not an edge detector. Input x; output step(x). Step(±0)=1; Step(+Infinity)=1 and Step(-Infinity)=+0. NaN produces NaN; all zero outputs are positive. Example: Step(-0.001)=0; Step(0)=1. |
